From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: GF intermittent partial generations — initial triage

Diego/Marissa/Sean — Alex reported three partial generations (gf-req-2142/2149/2156). I kicked off repro attempts against the same model and payloads. Summary so far below.

What I ran:
- Replayed their payloads against the hosted model variant (v1.3-q4) from our eu/us pools using the exact prompt and temperature.
- Captured token-level engine traces and KV cache behavior.
- Pulled CPU/GPU utilization and any trace logs for the request IDs in question.

Initial findings (attempts 1–8):
- We saw normal generation completion for all replays (full output returned) across both pools. No early termination in our traces.
- Token stream in the server logs shows the model generating the continued tokens; there are no gaps or snippet truncation on the host side.
- No upstream 5xx or restarts correlated with the timestamps.

Hypotheses to validate:
1) Client-side connection drop / early cancel (Greenfield reported no network errors but still possible).
2) SDK/HTTP proxy in front of Greenfield’s service terminating the stream on boundary conditions.
3) Rare model-decoder stall that only occurs under specific request timing — not reproduced yet.

Action items:
- Diego: can you run the engine-level trace extraction on the customer request ids (I attached request samples) and double-check whether the token stream for those request ids shows completion? Attach engine_traces_20280821.zip when done.
- Marissa: check our streaming proxy logs for any aborted connections or send window resets around the times Alex reported.
- Sean: please confirm if any autoscaling or maintenance activities overlapped that window.

I’ll keep Alex updated and escalate if we find server-side evidence.

— Ava

Attachments: repro_attempts_summary.md

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Greenfield] Intermittent missing paragraphs in final output — closure and findings

Hi Alex — apology for the delay and thanks again for the samples. We completed an internal triage and our conclusion is that we could not reproduce any server-side truncation for your reported requests. Summary below.

What we did:
- Replayed customer payloads against the same model variant and captured token-level server traces for the exact timestamps you provided. (See attached engine_traces_20280821.zip.)
- Reviewed streaming proxy logs and observed no aborted streams, 5xx, or transport resets correlated with the reported request ids.
- Checked autoscaling and infra events — no maintenance or restarts in the US pool during the incident window.
- Performed extended sampling for 72 hours to try to catch a similar failure mode; no occurrences.

Findings:
- Server traces: the model completed token emission for all replayed requests; there is no evidence of host-side early termination.
- Proxy logs: no connection aborts on our side. We did see a couple of short TCP retransmits (normal on the public internet) but nothing that would cause a stream to stop mid-sentence.
- Client correlation: the app trace you provided shows a session-level timeout at ~9s after stream start for gf-req-2149. That would result in the app dropping the connection and displaying a partial answer to the end-user.

Conclusion and recommended next steps:
- Conclusion: We were unable to confirm server-side truncation. The most likely root cause is a client-side timeout or intermediate proxy dropping the streaming connection.
- Recommendations for Greenfield:
  1) Increase client-side read timeout to 30s for this route while streaming (from current 10s).
  2) If you have an HTTP proxy or gateway in front of the app, check proxy send/idle timeouts and ensure streaming responses are allowed.
  3) If you can reproduce with the same request ids after adjusting timeouts, send us the full request/response capture (pcap or curl -v) and we’ll re-open a deeper trace.

Attachments included: engine_traces_20280821.zip, repro_attempts_summary.md, request_samples.txt

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute joint debug session to walk through a live replay. Please let me know preferred times and I’ll coordinate.

Thanks,
